title: Kajal Aggarwal Says South Cinema's Discipline Is What Bollywood Still Lacks
excerpt: The actress, who has worked across Telugu, Tamil, and Hindi films for nearly two decades, backs Deepika Padukone on work hours and draws firm personal boundaries on intimate scenes.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Kajal Aggarwal prefers South cinema for its discipline and structured work hours over Bollywood.
  • She supports Deepika Padukone's call for fixed working hours and limits her own shifts to nine hours.
  • Aggarwal maintains personal boundaries around intimate scenes, prioritizing comfort for her family.
  • She has starred in over 60 films across four languages, remaining a top actress in South cinema.
  • Upcoming projects include Ramayana: Part 1 and The India Story, showcasing her diverse roles.

Highest-Paid Actress in South Cinema
  • Kajal Aggarwal says she prefers the South film industry's ecosystem for its discipline, ethics, and structured work hours compared to Bollywood.
  • The actress has contract clauses limiting her to one nine-hour shift per day and has voiced support for Deepika Padukone's stance on fixed working hours.
  • Aggarwal, who has maintained personal boundaries around intimate scenes throughout her career, says the decision has not limited her professional growth.
  • She next appears in Ramayana: Part 1 opposite Yash and The India Story alongside Shreyas Talpade.

A Career Spanning Two Industries

https://youtube.com/watch?v=L98LuniufTM

Kajal Aggarwal has spent nearly two decades navigating the overlapping worlds of South Indian and Hindi cinema, building a career that includes Telugu blockbusters like Magadheera, Tamil hits like Thuppakki, and Bollywood projects opposite Ajay Devgn and Salman Khan. That cross-industry experience, the actress says, has given her a clear-eyed view of how the two ecosystems differ — and she has not been shy about which one she prefers.

"I prefer the ecosystem, the ethics, the values, the discipline of the South industry, which I feel is lacking in Hindi cinema," Aggarwal said at the News18 Rising India Summit.

"We don't work beyond nine hours. I have a slight preference for the South industry because that is where I started my career, and there is a certain comfort level that I don't find in Bollywood."

— Kajal Aggarwal, in an interview with Variety India

"I completely stand by her and I completely understand what she is saying," she said.

<p>The actress said motherhood has sharpened her own approach to work-life balance."

Standing With Deepika Padukone

Aggarwal's remarks have gained renewed traction amid an ongoing industry debate over working conditions, triggered by Deepika Padukone's reported exit from director Sandeep Reddy Vanga's film Spirit last year. Padukone was said to have sought fixed eight-hour work schedules and profit-sharing arrangements — demands that drew both support and pushback across Bollywood.

https://x.com/taran_adarsh/status/2079539804392567244

In a recent interview promoting her upcoming film The India Story, Aggarwal sided firmly with Padukone. "What happened to Deepika for asking for an eight-hour shift was not fair. I completely stand by her and I completely understand what she is saying," she said.

The actress said motherhood has sharpened her own approach to work-life balance. She now writes work-hour limitations into her contracts and works only one shift per day. "My priorities have shifted, and it has become more challenging. I want to return home at a specific hour," she told Variety India. She also noted that while she advocates structured schedules, filmmaking often requires adaptability. "In our industry, there are sometimes external factors that are beyond anyone's control, and you need to be adaptable," she added.

Personal Boundaries in an Industry Debate

›Limits work to one nine-hour shift daily.
›Prioritizes family comfort in film choices.

Aggarwal has also been vocal about the lines she draws around on-screen content, a position that has gained attention amid wider conversations about intimacy in Indian cinema. The actress reiterated her long-standing stance in a recent interview.

"Onscreen, I only did things I was comfortable with, or I would say that I cannot be a part of it, however important the role was," she said. "I refuse to do bikini scenes or intimate scenes because that is where I draw the line personally."

The position has remained consistent since her early Telugu career and carried through her Bollywood work. Aggarwal has said her family's comfort is a guiding principle — her films should be something her grandmother and parents can watch without discomfort. Despite those boundaries, she has delivered over 60 films across four languages and remains one of the highest-paid actresses in South Indian cinema.

A Packed Slate Ahead

Aggarwal, born and raised in Mumbai but now based between Hyderabad and Chennai, enters a busy stretch. She will portray Mandodari opposite Yash in the highly anticipated Ramayana: Part 1, and joins the ensemble cast for Kannappa alongside Akshay Kumar. Her food-adulteration drama The India Story, co-starring Shreyas Talpade, releases on July 24.

For the diaspora audience that has watched South Indian cinema gain global traction through RRR, Pushpa, and KGF, Aggarwal's comments capture a broader cultural shift. The work-culture differences she describes — punctuality, defined shifts, respect for boundaries — reflect part of why South productions have attracted top talent from across India's film landscape. Whether Bollywood absorbs the lesson is another matter. Aggarwal, approaching two decades in the business, is not waiting around to find out.
